Writing notes

Note view, the formatting toolbar, the / menu and everything you can put on a page.

#Notes and Pages are different documents

A Note is a quick, flowing page for ideas; a Page is a real document with margins, headers and page numbers. They are separate kinds — nothing switches by itself.

  1. Create either from New (top of the left bar) or the + button: Note, Page, Slides or Sheet.
  2. To turn a Note into a Page, use “Convert to a Page…” in the note’s File menu or panel; a Page has “Convert to a Note” in its panel. Each conversion makes a separate document.
  3. Pages are saved as real .docx files, so Word, Pages and Google Docs can open them.

Tip Use a Page for anything you will print, send or sign; use a Note for thinking, meeting notes and linked wiki pages.

#Formatting text

The floating toolbar has everything: styles, font, size, bold, italic, lists, colours, links, tables and pictures.

  1. Select text and use the toolbar, or right-click for a menu with size, colour, highlight and alignment.
  2. With nothing selected, choosing a font or size sets the page default.
  3. Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+K (link), Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y work as usual.

#The / menu

Type / at the start of a line to insert headings, lists, checklists, tables, columns, panels, code, diagrams, embeds and live blocks.

  1. Type / then a few letters to filter (for example “table” or “database”).
  2. Use ↑ ↓ and Enter to insert, Esc to close.

#Linking pages

Type [[ to link to another page, or @ to mention a page or a person.

  1. Type [[ and pick a page — or choose “Create …” to make a new one on the spot.
  2. A link always shows the page’s current title.
  3. Under every page, “Linked from” and “Links to” list its backlinks.

#Panels, columns, folding sections and more

Callout panels (info, note, success, warning, danger, decision), two or three columns, folding sections, a live contents list, code blocks and Mermaid diagrams.

  1. Insert them from the / menu.
  2. A code block has a language picker; choose “mermaid” to draw a diagram from text.
  3. A “Contents” block lists the page’s headings and updates as you write.

#Tables and pictures

Drag, align and wrap tables and pictures; paste screenshots straight in.

  1. Insert a table from the toolbar or the / menu; use the small toolbar that appears to add or remove rows and columns.
  2. Paste an image, or drop a file: it is stored inside the page.
  3. Drag a picture to move it; text wraps around it. Use its toolbar for alignment and wrapping.

#Comments

Select text and comment on it; reply, resolve or delete from the thread.

  1. Select text, then press Ctrl+Alt+M (or Insert → Comment).
  2. Click the highlighted text to open the thread.

#Find and replace

Search inside a page, or across all your pages.

  1. Ctrl+F searches the page you are on (case, whole word and regular expressions are options).
  2. Ctrl+Shift+H finds and replaces across every page. Tick which pages to change; a version of each is saved first.

#Types: Person, Meeting, Book…

Make a page “a Meeting” or “a Person” so it gets its own fields and starting template.

  1. Create a type from Databases → New type… (or Ctrl+Shift+P → “New type”): pick a starting point — Person, Meeting, Book, Project, Idea or blank — then name it and choose an icon and colour.
  2. Give a page a type with “+ Type” under its title (or Ctrl+Shift+P → “Page: make it a …”). Its fields appear under the title and are saved with the page; a page can have several types.
  3. Ctrl+Shift+P → “New Meeting” (etc.) starts a new page from the type’s template and name pattern (“Meeting — {date}”).
  4. Databases → Types lists every type with its pages as a table, board and more. Search with is:meeting to find pages of a type.

#Synced blocks

Write something once and show — and edit — it on as many pages as you like.

  1. Type /synced block for a new one, or /existing synced block to show one you made before (the list says how many pages use each).
  2. Or select text and right-click → Make this a synced block: it moves into a synced block and the same block can then be used elsewhere.
  3. Edit it on any page and every page that shows it changes at once. The header says how many pages use it.
  4. Unsync turns this copy into ordinary text (other pages keep the block); Remove takes it off this page but keeps the block.
  5. Exports and Page view write out the block’s current text. Tasks inside a synced block aren’t listed on the Tasks page.

#Fields inside text

Put a named value in a sentence — Budget: 1200 — and let search and lists read it.

  1. Type Budget:: (the word, two colons and a space) and press Space: it becomes a small field; type the value and press Enter. Or type /field.
  2. Click either half of the field to change the name or the value; Esc puts it back.
  3. Search for it: field:budget finds pages that have it, field:status=done matches a value, field:budget>1000 compares numbers or dates (also <, >=, <=).
  4. A search-results block shows the field’s value beside every page it finds.
  5. In Markdown files a field is written Budget:: 1200 (or [Budget:: 1200] inside a sentence) — the same as Obsidian’s Dataview.

#Search results and embedded pages

Live blocks that show a search, or part of another page, inside a page.

  1. Type /search results, then a search: words and operators such as label:design is:favourite in:Work -draft. Add type:task to list tasks. It updates by itself.
  2. Type /embed, choose a page and (optionally) one of its sections: the content is shown here, read-only, and follows the original — use Open to edit it there.
  3. Both are written out as plain text when you export or switch to Page view.

#Labels, status and owner

Give a page labels and properties, then find pages by them.

  1. Click “Add properties & labels” under the title (or ••• → Properties & labels…).
  2. Status can be Draft, In review, Approved or Archived. Add an owner and a date.
  3. Click a label anywhere to see every page that carries it.

#Templates

Start a page from meeting notes, a project plan, a decision record, a retrospective, a weekly review or a spec.

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+N, or use + → From template.
  2. To keep your own: ••• → Save as template… . It then shows in the template picker.

#Child pages and attachments

Nest pages under pages, and attach files to a page.

  1. ••• → Add child page, or Alt-drop a page onto another page in the left bar.
  2. Attach files from the Attachments box under a page; they stay with it.

#Version history

Doceo keeps earlier versions of every page.

  1. ••• → Version history… lists them.
  2. Restoring saves the current text first, so you can always come back.
  3. “Save a version now” in that window keeps one on purpose.

#Embeds, link cards and live blocks

Videos, designs, issues, other pages’ lists, calendars, task boards and databases can live inside a page.

  1. Paste a link to YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Figma, Google Docs / Sheets / Slides, or a GitHub issue to embed it; any other link on its own line becomes a preview card.
  2. Live blocks update by themselves: pages with a label, child pages, a properties report, a project’s tasks, an agenda, a task board and a database view (/database).
  3. Live blocks are written out as plain text and tables when you export or switch to Page view.
